ex.6: PNR distance is proportional to the fuel available: 880 × 11 000 / 10 000 = 968 NM.
ex.9: Minimum range = c × pulse length / 2 = 300 m/µs × 4 / 2 = 600 m.
ex.11: Azimuth resolution ≈ beam width × range = 3/60 × 60 NM = 3 NM.
ex.14: TOW limits: MTOW 72 000; MLW + burn-off 69 500; MZFW + fuel 70 000 → 69 500. Payload = 69 500 − 10 000 − 42 000 = 17 500 kg.
ex.15: Out: GS 265 kt at 255 lb/h. Back on one engine: GS 150 kt at 190 lb/h. d × (255/265 + 190/150) = 2500 → d ≈ 1122 NM.
ex.16: Book key prints (c). The radial is a great circle: initial track = 270° + ½ × 5° × sin 51° ≈ 271.9°T. Allow 7° starboard drift → TH ≈ 264.9°, + 8° W variation → about 273° M, so the correct answer is (a). The book's 271° ignores convergency.
ex.17: 5400 NM north from the equator is 90°: aircraft A is at the North Pole, which is due north (000°T) of anywhere.
ex.19: Bearing to the feature = 355 − 30 = 325° M = 340° T; the reciprocal (aircraft from feature) is 160° T.
ex.22: The aircraft is on QDR 150. Looking outbound along 140°, the 150 line is to the right, so turn left. On the 140 track outbound the RMI reads QDM 320°.
ex.30: LSS = 38.95 × √293 ≈ 667 kt (the book's 669 kt uses a rounded constant).
ex.31: 40 hPa × about 30 ft/hPa = 1200 ft; flying from high to low pressure with the same setting, the aircraft is lower than indicated.
ex.41: Book key prints (b). In air much warmer than ISA the altimeter under-reads, so an aircraft physically on the glide slope at the OM (true altitude 4200 ft) shows less than 4200 ft — the correct answer is (c).
ex.42: Book key prints (a). Jeppesen Grid MORA clears terrain and obstacles by 1000 ft where the highest elevations are 5000 ft MSL or lower and by 2000 ft where they are higher, so the correct answer is (c).
ex.45: 090° to 300° turning left is 150°; at 3° per second that takes 50 s.
ex.53: From 176°W westward across the date line to 177°E is 4° + 3° = 7° W.
ex.54: Setting 1013 with QNH 1008 over-reads by 5 × 27 ≈ 135 ft: 1240 + 135 = 1375 ft.
ex.55: QNH 10 hPa above standard: true altitude ≈ 7500 + 300 = 7800 ft; minus 1500 ft elevation = 6300 ft above the aerodrome.
ex.65: Heading = 085° M. The NDB bears 090 − atan(12/45) ≈ 075° M from the aircraft. Relative bearing = 075 − 085 = −10 → about 349°.
ex.68: The 60°N parallel is half the length of the equator, so B must fly twice as fast: 460 kt.
ex.71: 4 dots × 2° = 8°; at 45 NM, 8/60 × 45 = 6 NM. Fly right means the track is to the right, so the aircraft is left of it.
ex.73: Book key prints (c). It is the INS (mechanical gyros) that has many moving parts; the IRS (ring laser gyros) spins up faster but suffers from laser lock, so the correct answer is (a).
ex.76: Mercator scale varies with sec lat: 3 500 000 × cos 40° / cos 30° ≈ 1 : 3 096 000, which matches neither (a) nor (b) exactly.
ex.84: Beam half-width 2°. With the centre at +1° the lower edge (−1°) just touches the top: 1° at 60 NM ≈ 6000 ft → FL140. With the centre at −4° the upper edge (−2°) touches the base: 12 000 ft below → FL80.
ex.85: Lower edge of the beam = 4 − 2.5 = 1.5° above the horizontal. 70 NM × tan 1.5° × 6076 ft ≈ 11 100 ft.
ex.87: Minimum range = c × PW / 2 → PW = 2 × 0.125 × 1852 m / 300 m/µs ≈ 1.54 µs.
ex.88: One-way Doppler: v = Δf × c / f = 2015 × 3×10⁸ / 4.75×10⁹ ≈ 127 m/s ≈ 247 kt.
ex.90: Subtract the 50 µs transponder delay: 1950 µs / 12.36 µs per NM ≈ 158 NM.
ex.92: LSS = 480 / 0.82 ≈ 585 kt → T = (585 / 38.95)² ≈ 226 K = −47 °C, which is reached at about 31 500 ft in the ISA.
ex.93: ASDA = TORA + stopway = 2300 + 80 = 2380 m (clearway does not count).
ex.98: By 1225 A has flown 20 min × 370 = 123 NM, leaving 837 NM. Closing speed 660 kt → 76 min → 1341.
